output.reason: A 68-year-old with two weeks of worsening bilateral ankle swelling and two nights of orthopnea requiring sitting up to breathe suggests decompensating heart failure needing immediate emergency assessment with oxygen saturation, imaging and bloodwork today.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. Worsening swelling in both ankles plus needing to sit up to breathe at night can mean fluid backing up from a failing heart, which needs oxygen checks, a chest image and blood tests today. Do not drive yourself — have someone take you, or call 911 if breathing worsens, you get chest pain, or you feel faint.
differential: Decompensated heart failure with pulmonary and peripheral congestion
Other causes of fluid overload (kidney or liver disease)
